subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. 

Cut straight to the chase

options.text: Allow to introduce an unimportant part
Avoid unnecessary introduction and go to the more important part
Avoid the most important part of text
Disallow important introduction and go to the least important part

solution:
The correct answer is** "Avoid unnecessary introduction and go to the more important part "** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 Here we will learn the idiom with an example:

__
 
• **Cut straight to the chase* (idiom) *- **come to the point.

 
 
• ***Eg.** "Cut to the chase*—what is it you want us to do?"
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Let's learn some other idioms:

 
• **Cut straight to the point *(idiom) *- **Shorter and less ponderous

 
 
• ***Eg.*** Bernie was wildly successful here because he* cut straight to the point *and used a well-known, attention-grabbing phrase to send his message home.
